posts.title: Hyper-NA EUV: The Next Extension Beyond High NA Lithography (Carl Zeiss, ASML)
posts.summary:
Researchers at Carl Zeiss SMT and ASML published a technical paper titled “Hyper-NA: a system with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75.” Abstract Summary: The researchers examine Hyper-NA EUV lithography with a numerical aperture of at least 0.75 as a path beyond current 0.55-NA High-NA systems, including the optical architecture, resolution potential, reticle 3D... » read more
The post Hyper-NA EUV: The Next Extension Beyond High NA Lithography (Carl Zeiss, ASML) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from Carl Zeiss SMT and ASML have formally outlined the architecture for Hyper-NA EUV lithography, targeting a numerical aperture of at least 0.75.
This proposed technology serves as the successor to current 0.55-NA High-NA systems, aiming to push resolution limits further for future semiconductor nodes.

The technical paper addresses critical challenges for the next generation of lithography, including reticle 3D effects, polarization management, and the necessary expansion of the existing EUV ecosystem.

posts.title: Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics
posts.summary:
Increasing power density makes heat, stress, and aging harder to predict, and more critical to address earlier in the design flow.
The post Thermal Complexity Grows With AI Chips And Photonics appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Industry experts highlight that increasing power density in AI chips is making heat, stress, and aging significantly harder to predict, necessitating thermal management earlier in the design flow.

While photonics offers a path to reduce data center bottlenecks, the technology faces scalability hurdles and high sensitivity to heat, requiring complex control systems for thousands of integrated heaters.

The transition to heterogeneous architectures, such as co-packaged optics and mixed CPU/GPU environments, creates inconsistent thermal profiles that current cooling and design methodologies struggle to address.
Engineers are shifting toward modular, scalable architectures to mitigate losses and manage the thermal overhead inherent in high-performance computing systems.

posts.title: The Download: weight-loss drugs slowing aging and carbon dioxide batteries
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. Weight-loss drugs show signs of slowing biological aging, say drugmakers Popular weight-loss drugs may do more than help people shed pounds. They might also slow the aging process. Drugmakers Eli Lilly…
bullets: Eli Lilly and Novo Nordisk report that GLP-1 weight-loss drugs appear to slow biological aging markers, as measured by molecular 'aging clocks' tracking DNA and protein changes.

Energy Dome is scaling a novel energy storage solution that uses compressed carbon dioxide, offering a flexible alternative to traditional compressed-air systems that require specific geological formations.

OpenAI has published 377 new mathematical findings, signaling a continued push into automated scientific discovery that is creating significant disruption within the academic and research communities.

Former DeepMind researcher Thore Graepel argues that current large language models lack the genuine reasoning capabilities demonstrated by specialized systems like AlphaGo, challenging the prevailing narrative of AI progress.

posts.title: EU plans Chinese hybrid import curbs as test case for trade rebalancing, report says
posts.summary:
The EU is preparing safeguard measures targeting Chinese hybrids, potentially using tariff-rate quotas to limit imports, according to Bloomberg.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: The European Commission is developing safeguard measures to cap imports of China-made hybrid vehicles, marking a significant escalation in the ongoing automotive trade dispute.
Proposed mechanisms include tariff-rate quotas, which would impose levies on imports exceeding specific volume thresholds, serving as a potential template for broader trade rebalancing efforts.
This policy shift indicates the EU is moving toward unilateral import restrictions after China rejected previous requests for voluntary export restraints, citing WTO compliance concerns.

The outcome of upcoming high-level trade talks between EU Commissioner Maros Sefcovic and Chinese Commerce Minister Wang Wentao will be critical in determining the final scope and implementation of these measures.

posts.title: Apple and LG, The House For Everyone Else, Agent Standards and Amazon
posts.summary: Apple is taking a smarter approach to the home than I expected, leaning into integration (with partners); then, what Amazon should do about agents.
bullets: Apple is shifting its smart home strategy by prioritizing deep integration with third-party hardware partners like LG rather than attempting to manufacture every component in-house.
This collaborative approach suggests Apple is positioning its ecosystem as the central operating layer for the home, leveraging its software dominance to unify disparate hardware devices.

The analysis highlights a critical strategic pivot for Amazon, suggesting the company must establish clear standards for AI agents to maintain relevance as the smart home market evolves toward autonomous, agent-driven interactions.
By focusing on integration, Apple aims to capture the 'house for everyone else,' effectively competing against fragmented smart home ecosystems by providing a more cohesive user experience.
